content: Laboratory tests, such as monitoring potassium and sodium levels, may be conducted while you are using this medication. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is crucial to contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not skip doses without professional guidance. For proper storage of this medication, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the medication is expired or no longer needed, discard it appropriately. This information was last updated in August 2024. Please note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. This medication is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is also prescribed to prevent bacterial endocarditis (infection of the heart) in patients with certain heart conditions undergoing surgery. This medication belongs to the class of natural penicillin antibiotics. Depending on the specific product, this medication is administered via injection into a vein or muscle. Follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. Aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin) should be administered separately from this medication. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Common side effects may include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. If used to treat syphilis or other spirochetal infections (e.g., Lyme disease), this medication may cause a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, which typically occurs 1 to 2 hours after administration and can last up to 24 hours. Rarely, this medication may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., corn in products containing dextrose) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Penicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Some formulations of this medication contain sodium or potassium, which may be relevant for patients with specific dietary restrictions or medical conditions. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., specific urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function, complete blood count, potassium/sodium levels) may be conducted while you are using this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments.
